newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products market steady to firmer.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products market steady to firmer.

text.p: Singapore oil products prices were steady to firmer despite softer crudes, traders said.

Gas oil was mixed with paper slipping on weaker gas oil futures on London's IPE, while physical cargoes continued to be offered at firm levels. October swaps traded between $27.55 and $27.65, down from Wednesday's $27.75. An offer was seen for 220,000 barrels at $27.80 for September 29-October 1, while a S.Korean refiner offered at $28.10 fob. A bid was seen at $27.80 for early October. Offers on Wednesday were $27.50-$27.60. China's buying interest were at $214 a tonne c+f, but traders said China might lower it in anticipation of lower prices.
Taiwan bought its second jet fuel cargo by tender from Mobil at $247.82 a tonne c+f for October arrival. Taiwan bought the first cargo from Stinnes at $244.80.
Nepal has issued a tender to buy 30,000 tonnes of kerosene for October 1-15 arrival which closes on September 24.
The outlook on jet fuel prices seemed mixed as buyers and sellers differed on winter demand. Recent deals for prompt jet fuel was heard done at a 3-cent and 13-cents premium to Singapore quotes fob.
A physical bid was seen at $29.60 for Oct 1-5 with an offer at $30.35.

Naphtha edged up with crude while gasoline saw firm buying interest from a Singapore trader. Bids were raised through the day from $22.90, ending with two cargoes of 50,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded traded at $23.10 a barrel fob, lifting October 4-8 and 8-12. Traders said fundamentally the market has gained some support as September and October cargoes have moved out of Asia and Mideast to Africa, Mediterranean and possibly South America. Taiwan emerged for only one unleaded reformate cargo for November 1-20 delivery in a tender which closes September 24. But an official said if prices rose too high, CPC could drop the demand.--Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3093)
